transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I’ve been kind of planning my days around avoiding elevators. Like taking five flights of stairs at home, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I’ve also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another way up.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort when using an elevator?

Yeah… pretty much right away. Like if I’m walking toward one or I hear the doors clunk open, my chest tightens and my hands get sweaty. It’s just this quick rush of panic before I can really think about it.
Do you experience this kind of panic in other situations, like being in small rooms or high places?
I don’t think so… not really. I haven’t noticed it in small rooms or heights the same way. It’s mostly the elevator thing.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space that wasn't an elevator?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that happening, unless it’s an elevator.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space like a subway car or a tight room that isn't an elevator?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that with subway cars or rooms. It’s hard to say, but I don’t think it hits me the same way.
Have you ever felt anxious in a small, enclosed space that isn't an elevator?
Not that I can really remember. I mean, maybe I’d be a little uncomfortable, but I haven’t noticed it being a problem unless it’s an elevator.
Would your anxiety about elevators decrease if you were accompanied by a trusted person or someone who could help you
Maybe a little, I guess. I haven’t really paid close attention to that. It might help if someone was there, but… I’m not totally sure.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space like a car or a tight room that isn't an elevator?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think a car or tight room bothers me in the same way… at least I haven’t noticed it.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space like a tunnel?
I don’t really know. I don’t think tunnels bother me the same way, but I haven’t really paid much attention to it.
Do you feel anxious in small, enclosed spaces like a closet?
I’m not sure. I don’t really spend time in closets, so… I haven’t noticed feeling anxious there.
Do you feel anxious in small, enclosed spaces like a bathroom?
Bathrooms? Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t noticed feeling anxious in there.
Do you feel anxious in small, enclosed spaces like an MRI machine?
I don’t know, I’ve never had an MRI. I guess I’m not sure how I’d feel in one.
Have you ever felt anxious in a small, enclosed space that is not an elevator?
Not that I can think of. I mean, aside from elevators, I haven’t really noticed that happening.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small room with no windows and only one door?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been in that exact kind of room, or at least I haven’t noticed getting anxious about it.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space like a ship cabin?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been in a ship cabin, so I don’t know how I’d react.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space like a submarine?
I don’t really know. I’ve never been in a submarine, so… hard to say.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space with someone you trust?
I don’t know… maybe less so if it was someone I trusted, but I’m not really sure.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space with no way out, other than an elevator?
I’m not really sure. I guess having no way out sounds uncomfortable, but I don’t know how anxious I’d actually get.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space with no windows and only one door, without any possibility of using an elevator?
I’m not sure. I mean, no windows and one door doesn’t sound great, but I don’t really know how I’d react.
Would you feel anxious if you were in a small room with no windows and only one door, and there was no elevator?
I’m not really sure. I think it might feel a little uncomfortable, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly.
